assertion: This ties for the fifth-largest raise over the last 35 years.

assertion: it's the sixth straight year in which payouts have risen by at least 2.5%, which is something that hasn't been witnessed since the late 20th century (1988-1997).

Social Security raises of 3.2% (2024), 2.5% (2025), and 2.8% (2026) were met by Medicare Part B premium hikes of 5.9% (2024), 5.9% (2025), and 9.7% (2026). In 2026, the standard monthly premium for Part B is $202.90

assertion: A larger-than-normal annual COLA can drain the OASI's already declining asset reserves even faster. This means the projected timeline to benefit cuts may now be less than six years away, and the needed reduction could ultimately be larger than 22%.
inaccuracy: No estimate offered; the Trustees date is already Q4 2032 (about six years), and higher inflation also raises wages and payroll revenue, so the net effect of one COLA is unquantified
why_not: The Fool Oct 4 page repeats 22% and 'six years' but offers no estimate linking the COLA to a larger cut; the 22% figure itself is the Trustees' number and is graded true in the claim above.
